sections.value: I am Christian Schuler, a PhD candidate in Computational Linguistics at Saarland University (UdS), affiliated with the German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI), specifically the Department of Multilinguality and Language Technology (MLT). Under the supervision of Prof. Dr. Josef van Genabith, Prof. Dr. Timo Baumann, and Dr. Simon Ostermann, I work on Dialect-Aware Natural Language Processing for Low-Resource Languages. My current research focuses on developing robust techniques for language identification (LID) and automatic speech recognition (ASR), with an initial emphasis on Kurdish varieties.

More broadly, I am interested in how dialect-aware and multilingual NLP can support linguistic diversity, improve the accessibility of language technologies, and strengthen cross-cultural communication. Guided by the motto 生于忧患，死于安乐 (“We survive in adversity, we perish in ease and comfort”), I believe that focusing primarily on high-resource languages like English risks leaving our field fragile and incomplete. My work therefore seeks to build more resilient and inclusive language technologies by tackling the challenges of low-resource and dialectal settings. This motivation builds upon my previous research: my Master’s thesis, “Leveraging Morphological and Lexical Features in Synthetic Data Generation for Dialect-Specific Machine Translation” (supervised by Dr. Sina Ahmadi, Dr. Seid Muhie Yimam, and Prof. Dr. Chris Biemann), and my Bachelor’s thesis, “Perceptual Quality Assessment of Lip-Synchrony in Dubbing” (supervised by Prof. Dr. Timo Baumann and Prof. Dr. Timo Gerkmann), which first sparked my interest in the interplay between language and technology.

I enjoy applying computational methods to real-world problems at the intersection of linguistics, AI, and society. I welcome collaborations on research projects, interdisciplinary initiatives, and practical applications in these areas. Feel free to reach out if you are interested in discussing ideas or doing your thesis on a related topic.
